title: Inside orch
subtitle: Building and Operating a Docker Orchestrator in Go
author: Aleksandar Popovic
description: A source-based engineering study of orch: Go control planes, Docker workers, state ownership, scheduling, failure recovery, and the limits of executable integration.
copyright: Copyright © 2026 Aleksandar Popovic. All rights reserved. No new public license is granted for the original manuscript. Source excerpts and third-party materials retain their existing rights and notices.
lab_status: All eight laboratories independently rerun; scope and actual command records retained under validation/labs/review076. Fake-runtime, guarded Docker, and full-schema PostgreSQL observations remain distinct.
word_count_method: Markdown inline text and technical identifiers; no fenced code/output, URL destinations, build metadata or duplicated unified export. Separate lab guides reported but excluded from the editorial target.
publication_state: Prepared and verified locally; no push, deployment, ISBN, endorsement, or production certification claimed.

cover.alt: Inside orch: Building and Operating a Docker Orchestrator in Go, by Aleksandar Popovic. Navy cover with cyan title and the Orch vector mark.

audience: Go and API developers tracing concrete state transitions and contracts
Operators investigating task, agent, rollout, secret and recovery evidence
Architects comparing state ownership, consistency, leadership and integration boundaries
prerequisites: Ability to read Go and command-line procedures; disposable source copy at the pinned revision
Go 1.25.0 and cached module dependencies for source-based experiments
Docker or PostgreSQL only for the specifically guarded laboratories that require them; never reset shared services
learning_outcomes: Trace accepted service intent through task assignment, reports and Docker operations
Distinguish deterministic placement and per-task claims from global capacity reservation
Measure recovery, rollout and admission behavior with bounded actual evidence
Identify memory-only default state, omitted resource propagation and unwired packages before making reliability claims

reader_paths.developer: Domain models → HTTP/CLI → scheduling/reconciliation → jobs → executable contracts
reader_paths.operator: Process restart → agents → rollout/drain → secret custody → bounded database recovery
reader_paths.architect: State ownership → assignment races → namespaces → leadership → composition gaps

social.title: Inside orch — engineering a Go/Docker orchestrator
social.description: Forty source-based chapters, six appendices, worked answers and eight bounded laboratories. Read the implementation and its failure limits.
